title: Multi-tenant Seasonal Credits & Soft-Overage Policy for Burst Plans
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Several enterprise customers requested predictable ways to run seasonal marketing campaigns and temporary usage bursts without triggering hard overage billing and without manually adjusting plan entitlements. Current plan models only support fixed monthly quotas, per-route quotas, and hard overage charges. We need a first-class mechanism for: (1) issuing time-bounded 'seasonal credits' that consume quota but do not immediately invoice overage, and (2) a soft-overage policy that notifies, throttles gently, and optionally pauses non-critical routes prior to hard billing.

Goals:
- Provide product teams and account managers an API + Console flow to grant seasonal credits to specific tenants, routes, or keys.
- Ensure credits are visible in Console with rollup and per-route breakdown and are applied before any overage calculation.
- Implement a soft-overage path: warning notifications, configurable soft-throttle thresholds, policy-driven route deprioritization, and a 72-hour grace window before hard billing consumes core quota.
- Ensure billing reconciliation and invoices reflect credits applied and any hard overage after grace window.

Non-goals:
- This work does not redesign subscription tiers or seat-based billing.
- We will not implement automated credit sales or marketplace purchase flows in this phase.

Context & Rationale: Marketing teams often coordinate limited-time promotions or partner events where traffic spikes 3–10x for 48–96 hours. Manual quota increases are slow and error-prone; immediate hard overage billing causes customer friction. A credit+soft-overage model reduces churn risk while preserving cost controls for Redwood.

requirements: Credits must be time-bound (start_time, end_time) and targetable at tenant, project, API key, and route levels
Credits are consumed prior to any quota deduction and should be visible in usage streams and Console line-items
Soft-overage threshold is configurable per-tenant and per-plan; default is 100% of quota triggers warnings and 110% triggers soft-throttle
Soft-throttle should degrade non-critical routes (user-specified) first and preserve a critical_minimum for emergency endpoints
A 72-hour configurable grace window begins once soft-overage policy engages; customers get automated email/slack alerts and console banners
If soft-overage persists beyond grace window, remaining usage is billed as hard overage at plan-defined rates and shown on next invoice
APIs for Account Admins: create_credit, list_credits, revoke_credit, credit_impact_preview (simulate application)
Console flows: grant credit (UI), view credit balance & consumption timeline, soft-overage policy settings, notification center entries
Billing engine change: credits must be recorded as distinct line-items (credit-apply events) and included in metering exports for reconciliation
Telemetry: emit metrics for credit consumption rate, soft-overage activations, routes deprioritized, and grace-window expirations
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end scenario: Create a 7-day credit of 500k tokens at tenant level; run sample workload that would exceed base quota; credit is consumed first and Console shows credit consumption timeline

Soft-overage activation: Configure soft-overage at 100%/110%; trigger run causes warning banner, email to admin, and non-critical routes return 429 with X-Redwood-Throttle-Reason=soft_overage after threshold
Grace window behavior: Soft-overage persists for 72 hours; system charges remaining usage as overage at next invoice; invoice contains credit line-items and clear notation of grace window start/end
API surface: create_credit/list_credits/revoke_credit endpoints accept and return documented fields and error codes; credit_impact_preview matches Console projection within 2% for synthetic workloads
Telemetry & QA: Dashboard shows credit consumption metric; at least two Grafana panels and one alert (soft-overage active > 1h) added to Console monitoring
Security & Billing: No PII in credit metadata; KMS encryption applies to credit issuance records where required by compliance; billing export contains a credit_id for reconciliation
Performance: Applying a credit to a tenant with 10k active routes adds < 50ms median request-path decision latency at the routing layer
Docs & Support: Runbook and support playbook published; two support engineers trained and playbook validated in a mock incident
success_metrics: Reduction in manual quota change requests by enterprise customers for short-term campaigns by >= 60% within 3 months
Customer-reported billing disputes related to short-term spikes reduced by >= 50% for pilots
80% of pilot customers use the Console flow to grant seasonal credits vs asking Sales/CS
No increase in overall bad debt attributable to credits above 0.5% of monthly revenue during pilot
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Pilot): Implement credit data model, API endpoints, billing export changes, and Console grant/view screens for 5 pilot tenants (billing-2026.04)
Phase 2 (Policy + Soft-throttle): Add soft-overage engine, notification integrations (email/Slack), and route deprioritization hooks (billing-2026.05)
Phase 3 (GA): Harden reconciliation, multi-region awareness, self-serve UI for Sales/CS and expanded telemetry (billing-2026.07)
Pilot onboarding: coordinate with CS for 5 pilot customers, produce sample SQL for finance reconciliation, and schedule weekly syncs during pilot
notes_and_decisions: Decision: Credits are not refundable once consumed; unconsumed portion may be revoked and optionally converted to account credit at Finance discretion
Decision: Soft-overage default thresholds chosen conservatively (100% warn / 110% soft-throttle) to avoid surprise billing
Trade-off: Implementing route-level deprioritization requires lightweight runtime hooks; initial approach uses a header-based signal (X-Redwood-Priority) to preserve performance
Open question: Whether to allow stacking of credits with reserved capacity discounts; dependency flagged to finance (PM-24107)
Link to prototype PR for billing export changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-prototypes/pull/92
